units.title: Sounds & numbers
units.goal: Read Creole spelling aloud and count.

rule.h: Read it the way it sounds
rule.x: Each letter always makes the same sound. é is the ay in pay, è the e in let, ou the oo in fool. u and œ are the French sounds in sûr and sœur. A vowel before n or m in the same syllable (an, en, in, on, un) is nasal: say it through your nose and drop the n. ch is the ch in church, sh the sh in sheep, j the s in treasure.
rule.fr: Nasal vowels, u and œ work as in French, but the spelling is phonetic: every letter is said.

units.title: Introductions & greetings
units.goal: Greet someone, say how you are, and give your name.

rule.x: Subject pronouns: je (I), to (you), li (he, she, it), no (we), vou or vouzòt (you all), yé (they). After a verb, 'me' is mò or mwa and 'you' is twa: Li dòn mò ça. Put mwa, twa or li at the start or end to stress who you mean.
rule.fr: Like French je and moi, tu and toi: a short form before the verb, a strong form on its own. É twa? is Et toi? The verb never changes with the person.

units.title: Where are you from? What do you do?
units.goal: Say where you are from and what you do.

rule.x: With a describing word you need no verb at all: Je fim, I'm hungry. To link two nouns, use çé: Je çé étidyan. When a question ends on 'to be', use yê: Éyou to yê?
rule.fr: English says I am hungry; Creole says I hungry. Çé works like French c'est.

units.title: Birthdays & age
units.goal: Give your age and birthday, and compare people.

rule.x: Gin means have, and age uses it: je gin swasant zan, I'm sixty. For the age you are turning, use fé: Je fé kinz zan. Compare with pli ... ke (more ... than), mwins ... ke (less ... than) and osi ... ke (as ... as).
rule.fr: French j'ai soixante ans is je gin swasant zan, and plus ... que is pli ... ke.
ex: Je pli vyé ke twa; je gin swasant zan.
I'm older than you; I'm sixty years old.
Non, je osi smat ke twa!
No, I'm as smart as you!

units.title: Family, this & that, one & many
units.goal: Talk about your family and point things out.

rule.x: -la after a noun means the: fenm-la. In means a. -yé after a noun makes a specific plural: mô frær-yé. Possessives go before the noun: mô, tô, sô, nô, vô, yê. -çila means this and -çala that. Dê means some.
rule.fr: The comes after the noun (lamézon-la, not la maison), and nouns have no gender.
ex: My brothers don't live here anymore.
Je mèt dê tomat dan mô gombo.
I put some tomatoes in my gumbo.

units.title: Home & where is it?
units.goal: Find things in a house and say what you don't do.

rule.x: In the present, pa goes after the verb: Li manj pa lavyònn. In the simple past it goes before: Li pa manjé lavyònn. With konné, olé, gin, bezwin and kapab it always goes before. After té, va or sé it comes right after the marker. Jamé is never, pærsonn no one, aryin nothing, nil-plas nowhere.
rule.fr: One word, pa, does the job of French ne ... pas.
ex: He didn't see anyone. (He saw no one)

units.title: Weather & outdoors
units.goal: Describe the weather and what is outside.

rule.x: Weather uses li fé with no real subject: Li fé sho, li fé fré. Ina means there is or there are: Ina in ta nwaj. A lot of weather is just a noun and a verb: Lapli tomb.
rule.fr: Li fé sho is French il fait chaud, and ina is il y a.
ex: Ina in ta nwaj dan syèl-la.
There's a lot of clouds in the sky.

units.title: Time, routines & the past
units.goal: Talk about your week and what you did.

rule.x: Té before a verb puts it in the past: Je té dòrmi, I was sleeping or I had slept. For a plain past, use the long form with no marker: Nouzòt parlé françé, we spoke French (parl is now, parlé was). State verbs like gin, olé, kapab and bezwin always take té for the past.
rule.fr: Nothing to conjugate: one small word in front, for every person.
ex: Je té dòrmi tandi to té kwi soupé.
I was sleeping while you were cooking supper.

units.title: Likes, dislikes & hobbies
units.goal: Say what you like doing and ask others.

rule.x: Many verbs have a short form (parl) and a long form (parlé). Use the short form for the plain present. Use the long form after linm, olé, té, va and sé, and for the simple past. The present also covers -ing: Li lir in liv, he reads or he is reading.
rule.fr: I like to fish is Je linm péshé: no 'to', and no separate -ing form.
ex: Je linm péshé kan je gin tem.
I like to fish when I have time.
What do you like to do?

units.title: Clothes & body parts
units.goal: Say what you wear and whose things are whose.

rule.x: Add -chin, -kin, -chènn or -kènn to a possessive to say my own or mine: mô-chènn mézon, my own house. On its own it means mine, yours, hers: Çé sô-chènn. Body parts just take the possessive: mô pyé-yé, my feet.
rule.fr: Tô-kin and mô-kin work like French le tien and le mien.
ex: Tô-kin çé pli gran ke mô-kin.
Je mèt shapo, jakèt, kilot, èk in pær bòt.
I wear a hat, jacket, pants and a pair of boots.

units.title: Health, sickness & myself
units.goal: Say what hurts and how you feel.

rule.x: For myself, herself and so on, add -minm to the pronoun: Je lav mo-minm, Li parl a li-minm. Pain uses fé mal: Mô lèstoma fé mal. You can also say je gin mal- plus the body part.
rule.fr: French se laver is lav mo-minm, and ça fait mal is fé mal.
ex: Mô lèstoma fé mal; je gin mal-lèstoma.
My stomach hurts; I have a stomach ache.

units.title: Invitations, questions & excuses
units.goal: Invite someone, ask questions, and say no politely.

rule.x: A question keeps the same word order: raise your voice, or start with èske. Question words go first: ki (who, which), kwa (what), éyou (where), kan (when), kòfær (why), komen (how). Olé, bezwin, kapab and gin pou take the long form of the next verb: T'olé manjé?
rule.fr: Èske is French est-ce que. There is no 'do' as in English Do you ...?
ex: I need to go to the grocery store.
To gin pou kouri shé twa.

units.title: Travel, directions & the future
units.goal: Plan a trip and say what you will do.

rule.x: Va or a before the long form makes the future: J'a wa mô sœr, To va fé ça? Kouri or alé before a verb means going to. P'alé is the negative: Je p'alé gété TV. For will be, use sa: Je sa la talœr.
rule.fr: Like English going to, or French je vais plus a verb.
ex: I'm not going to watch TV today.

rule.x: Si means if. Sé before the long form means would: Li sé kwi soupé, he would cook supper. Si plus the present, then va for what will happen. Si plus té, then sé for what would happen.
rule.fr: Sé does the job of French -rais endings (je mangerais), as one separate word.
ex: Si yé vyin aswa, li sé kwi soupé pou yé.
If they come this evening, he'd cook supper for them.
Si tem-la jlé, yé va gin laglas.
If it's freezing, there will be ice.
Je sé linmé, mé mô tèt fé mal.
I'd love to, but my head hurts.
She should be able to do it.

units.title: Music, dancehall & courting
units.goal: Describe people and places with longer sentences.

rule.x: Ki joins a description to a noun: in kouzin ki travay o Téksas. Often you need nothing: nom-la je jwènn iyær, the man I met yesterday. Ça ki means what: Li manjé ça ki je kwi. Éyou joins a place: bayou éyou no fé lashash.
rule.fr: Ki is French qui or que, and ça ki is ce qui or ce que.
ex: Je gin in kouzin ki travay o Téksas.
I have a cousin who works in Texas.
Li manjé ça ki je kwi.
She ate what I cooked for her.
The bayou where we go hunting.

units.title: Farming, garden & animals
units.goal: Give instructions and talk about animals and crops.

rule.x: For a command, use the short form on its own: Donn mò kishòj, Parl kréyol. Pa after it makes don't: Marsh pa dan labou. For be, use dèt: Dèt pa tar!
rule.fr: As in English, a command has no subject.
ex: Alòr, marsh pa dan labou, padna.
Well then don't walk in the mud, friend.

units.title: Cooking, food & describing
units.goal: Describe food and say how you cook it.

rule.x: Most describing words come after the noun: in shyin las. A few, for beauty, age, newness, goodness and size, come before: in gran lamézon, in bon tem. Byin, jolimen, tro and mòyær go before a describing word to make it stronger: byin kanay.
rule.fr: Mostly as in French: une grande maison, but un chien fatigué.
ex: To linm tô manjé byin sézonné?
Do you like your food well seasoned?

units.title: Holidays: putting it together
units.goal: Talk about holidays using everything so far.

rule.x: Word order is subject, verb, object, as in English: Je linm twa, to linm mwa. Markers go before the verb in a fixed order: té (past), va (future) or sé (would), then pa, then the verb: No té pa kapab vini.
rule.fr: Same order as English; only the little markers are new.
ex: N'a gin in bon tem pou Mardi Gra-la!
We're going to have a good time for Mardi Gras!
